description: Routing scenarios for a constitutional writ petition heard on the record. These do not score legal quality — they check that the proceeding-type model actually holds: that no objection is screened where no ground applies, that no witness testifies where there is no witness box, and that the right agent answers in each phase.
whyStructuralNotJudged: Every other courtroom metric grades a decision the model made. These grade the graph. A writ engages none of the seven evidentiary grounds in the corpus, so 'counsel did not object' is not a model opinion that could be right or wrong — it is an invariant, and any violation is a routing bug. Structural checks are the only honest way to measure that, and they are cheap: one model call per scenario.

case.title: Asma Bibi v. Board of Revenue
case.summary: Constitutional petition under Article 199 challenging executive revenue circulars that deny female heirs equal mutation rights in ancestral agricultural land. The petitioner says the circulars require a no-objection certificate from male co-sharers before mutation, which no statute authorises.
case.applicableLaws: Const. 1973 Art. 4 (Right of individuals to be dealt with in accordance with law, etc.), Const. 1973 Art. 25 (Equality of citizens), Const. 1973 Art. 199 (Jurisdiction of High Court)

witnesses.name: Salim Tehsildar
witnesses.statement: The mutation was deferred pending a no-objection certificate from the male co-sharers, per provincial administrative instructions.

witnessFixtureNote: The case file deliberately still carries a witness. A generated writ has none, but a session created before proceeding types existed does, and a stale activeWitness must not seat someone in a proceeding that has no stand. Scenario writ_stale_witness is that adversarial case.

scenarios.utterance: My Lord, this petition is maintainable under Article 199. The impugned circulars require a no-objection certificate that no statute authorises, and they operate only against female heirs.
scenarios.rationale: Opening submissions are made to the bench; the court responds.

scenarios.utterance: The respondent has no answer to Article 25. A classification that burdens only female heirs is not a reasonable classification.
scenarios.rationale: Submissions is where the respondent answers the petition, so opposing counsel replies.

scenarios.utterance: My Lord, the alternate remedy under the revenue hierarchy is not adequate because the circular binds every forum below this Court.
scenarios.rationale: The bench puts its own questions to counsel and receives the answer.

scenarios.utterance: For these reasons the circulars are ultra vires Article 4 and discriminatory under Article 25, and the petition should be allowed.
scenarios.rationale: Closing is addressed to the bench.

scenarios.utterance: You accept, do you not, that the Board issued this circular knowing full well it would strip women of their inheritance?
scenarios.rationale: Blatantly leading, and put as if to a witness. In a trial this draws an objection under Arts. 136-138. In a writ there is no witness and no examination, so no ground is engaged and counsel simply answers the point.

scenarios.utterance: Mr. Tehsildar, you deferred the mutation because the male co-sharers objected, didn't you?
scenarios.rationale: A stale activeWitness from before proceeding types existed. A writ has no stand, so nobody is seated and nobody testifies, however the request is shaped.
